question: Part III of the Constitution of India stated about which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Part III of the Constitution of India deals with **Fundamental Rights**, which are enshrined from Article 12 to 35.
 
• These rights are considered essential for the all-around development of individuals and are applicable to all citizens of India.
 
• Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning they are enforceable by the courts, and individuals can approach the courts in case of any violation.
 
• They include rights such as the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• These rights act as a safeguard against any arbitrary actions of the state and ensure protection of individual liberties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Equality**

 
 
• It includes equality before the law, prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• It also includes equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and abolition of untouchability and titles.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom**
 
 
• It includes the freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and the right to practice any profession or occupation.
 
• These freedoms are subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the state in the interest of sovereignty, integrity, and public order.
 
 
 
• **Right against Exploitation**
 
 
• This right prohibits all forms of forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking.
 
• It aims to protect individuals from exploitation and abuse.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion**
 
 
• It guarantees religious freedom to all citizens and ensures secularism in the country.
 
• Individuals are free to profess, practice, and propagate any religion of their choice.
 
 
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies**
 
 
• This right allows individuals to approach the Supreme Court or High Courts for enforcement and protection of their Fundamental Rights.
 
• It acts as a guardian of all other Fundamental Rights.
